title: Reliability, Risk, and Escalation
summary: Trace dependencies and decide when a risk needs escalation.
objectives: Identify dependencies and possible failure domains.
Connect redundancy, maintenance, and escalation to reliability.

vocab.def: A part of a system that can fail together.
The possibility that an event could cause harm or loss.

sections.heading: Systems depend on systems
sections.body: A service may depend on compute, network, power, cooling, and procedures. A local fault can have a wider effect, so evidence and handoffs matter.

sections.heading: Reliability is managed
sections.body: Backups, monitoring, maintenance, controlled changes, and escalation reduce risk. They do not guarantee that every failure can be prevented.

practice.prompt: A network path has one link and a backup power path has two. Which design has fewer single points of failure?
practice.answer: The backup power path, because it has another available path.

quiz.question: Why should a possible cascading risk be escalated?
options: Another authorized team may need to coordinate the response
It guarantees there is no failure
quiz.answer: Another authorized team may need to coordinate the response

lab.objective: Trace a synthetic dependency chain and identify a safe escalation point.

reflectionPrompt: Which dependency would you want documented before making a change?
